comment.narrative: Component 1The Macroprudential Policy Strategy was developed. The document was approved within the National Committee for Financial Stability on 15 September 2023. Two subcomponents of the stresstest modules were defined and are ready to use. Another component model has been developed and some additional toolboxes were purchased and the program was installed. An adaptation of the contagion model presented by the NBR STE on NBMs local data developed by the NBR STE in Matlab was done. An Action Plan for improving the quality of the FSR encompassing all the recommendations provided by the STEs during their missions was prepared. The NBM Board has approved the improved Financial Stability Report on the 8th of June 2023 and published on the NBM website on 15 June 2023.Component 2The assessment of the draft primary legislations on insurance regarding the compliance with the EU Solvency II Directive and on mandatory motor third party liability insurance regarding the compliance with EU Motor Insurance Directive and related framework was done. The drafting process on the NBM primary and secondary legislation in order to adapt to Solvency II Directive and MTPL Directives requirements is ongoing. The format of the missions along with the training are designed in order for the beneficiary instititution staff to address questions exchange best practices and gain knowledge. ASF experts assisted NBM in drafting a secondary regulatory framework for the external audit of the financial statements of the insurance companies including provisions regarding the endorsement of the auditing entity and the relation between the auditor and the audited entity andor financial supervisor. A draft of Risk Assessment Framework has been developed. NBM will prepare an initial draft of requirementsmethodology for insures undertakings stress tests.Component 3Necessary methodologies and supervisory tools were developed and enforced including guidelines for assessing the transparency of the ownership structure of the NBCOs and updating of information about founders ultimate beneficiaries regulation on responsible lenging offsite supervision internal procedure the Instruction regarding the financial reporting of nonbank lending organizations. Assessment was done for the fit proper criteria for administrators of NBCOs and criteria in this regard has been introduced in the primary law that amend the Law nr.12018 on NBCOs. NBM representatives have been trained during the missions dedicated to the capacity building of the NBM staff including through study visits. NCFM experts together with representatives of the Consumer Protection Agency have examined the best EU practices presented by the Romanian colleagues in the field of the analysis of unfair practices used by the traders in their relations with individual consumers. NBR STE presented the methodology for onsite inspections and offsite risk based supervision of NBCOs with the focus on AMLCFT. Component 4A number of 3 primary laws were amended and were approved on October 19 2023 by the Parliament of Moldova. A number of 7 secondary level normative acts were developed and almost all of them were already approved. All relevand staff responsbile with oversight was trained. STEs provided comprehensive presentations and guides on all aspects of oversight to all the NBM oversight staff. Detailed methodologiesinternal procedures to perform oversight following EU best practices were provided and elaborated.Component 5A comprehensive analysis of the State of Play in Moldova and the necessary steps to adhere to SEPA was done. A questionnaire in order to assess the level of interest and the readiness of the market players to adhere to SEPA was elaborated. An Action Plan with milestones and deadlines for adhering to SEPA was established and approved by NBM.The Application for adherence to SEPA was finalized and will be submitted by the NBM to the European Payment Council.

comment.narrative: By 31 may 2022 the Twinning Project team has continued to provide inputs in achieving the overall objective. Notably completion of the subresults 2.1 and 2.2 of the twinning fiche respectively the assessment of the draft primary legislation on insurance regarding the compliance with EU Solvency II Directive and related framework along with the assessment of the draft primary legislation on mandatory motor third party liability insurance regarding the compliance with EU Motor Insurance Directive resulting in a Gap Analysis Action Plan for the harmonization of the Moldovan legislative framework with the European requirements in the insurance area. In the context of activity 3.7 technical support in developing a methodology of a riskbased supervision of NBCOs in the areas of prevention and combating money laundering and terrorist financing was provided by presenting NCFM the model of methodology of a riskbased supervision of NBCOs which remains to be adapted by NCFM giving the country particularities. Subresult 5.1. was completed by providing an analysis of the state of play in Moldova and necessary steps for adhering to SEPA as well as other materials in respect to all components of the twinning project like training materials provided and assistance for NBMs staff delivered for designing a Macroprudential Policy Strategy GAP analysis prepared and recommendations prepared together with the NCFM staff in respect of necessary methodologies regulatory and supervisory tools under the new legal framework primary and secondary legislation for nonbank credit organisations training materials provided and assistance for calibrating debtservicetoincome and loantovalue limits structuring the Financial Stability Report as well as the framework to analyze household and nonfinancial companies sector presentations recommendations in respect to regulation of the financial market infrastructions questionnaire to address issues to payment service providers on fees for payments in euro and the infrastructure used to process these type of payments also to target the time needed to implement technical requirements for SEPA payments ISO20022 constrains and real commitment of the banks to adhere to SEPA as well as other materials in respect to all components of the twinning project. The activities of the project have been designed to support the achievement of the overall objective and its indicator and MS and BC partners are committed to support this process. During the technical assistance missions provided in the reporting period aspects related to institutional capacity are being taken into consideration from the perspective of sharing best practices and knowledge aiming to identify the best ways for the implementation of the experts recommendations. This is a step implemented before the dedicated trainings specifically addressed to institutional capacity will follow in the next period of implementation.

comment.narrative: Component 1The Macroprudential Policy Strategy was developed. The document was approved within the National Committee for Financial Stability on 15 September 2023. Two subcomponents of the stresstest modules were defined and are ready to use. Another component model has been developed and some additional toolboxes were purchased and the program was installed. An adaptation of the contagion model presented by the NBR STE on NBMs local data developed by the NBR STE in Matlab was done. An Action Plan for improving the quality of the FSR encompassing all the recommendations provided by the STEs during their missions was prepared. The NBM Board has approved the improved Financial Stability Report on the 8th of June 2023 and published on the NBM website on 15 June 2023.Component 2The assessment of the draft primary legislations on insurance regarding the compliance with the EU Solvency II Directive and on mandatory motor third party liability insurance regarding the compliance with EU Motor Insurance Directive and related framework was done. The drafting process on the NBM primary and secondary legislation in order to adapt to Solvency II Directive and MTPL Directives requirements is ongoing. The format of the missions along with the training are designed in order for the beneficiary instititution staff to address questions exchange best practices and gain knowledge. ASF experts assisted NBM in drafting a secondary regulatory framework for the external audit of the financial statements of the insurance companies including provisions regarding the endorsement of the auditing entity and the relation between the auditor and the audited entity andor financial supervisor. A draft of Risk Assessment Framework has been developed. NBM will prepare an initial draft of requirementsmethodology for insures undertakings stress tests.Component 3Necessary methodologies and supervisory tools were developed and enforced including guidelines for assessing the transparency of the ownership structure of the NBCOs and updating of information about founders ultimate beneficiaries regulation on responsible lenging offsite supervision internal procedure the Instruction regarding the financial reporting of nonbank lending organizations. Assessment was done for the fit proper criteria for administrators of NBCOs and criteria in this regard has been introduced in the primary law that amend the Law nr.12018 on NBCOs. NBM representatives have been trained during the missions dedicated to the capacity building of the NBM staff including through study visits. NCFM experts together with representatives of the Consumer Protection Agency have examined the best EU practices presented by the Romanian colleagues in the field of the analysis of unfair practices used by the traders in their relations with individual consumers. NBR STE presented the methodology for onsite inspections and offsite risk based supervision of NBCOs with the focus on AMLCFT. Component 4A number of 3 primary laws were amended and were approved on October 19 2023 by the Parliament of Moldova. A number of 7 secondary level normative acts were developed and almost all of them were already approved. All relevand staff responsbile with oversight was trained. STEs provided comprehensive presentations and guides on all aspects of oversight to all the NBM oversight staff. Detailed methodologiesinternal procedures to perform oversight following EU best practices were provided and elaborated.Component 5A comprehensive analysis of the State of Play in Moldova and the necessary steps to adhere to SEPA was done. A questionnaire in order to assess the level of interest and the readiness of the market players to adhere to SEPA was elaborated. An Action Plan with milestones and deadlines for adhering to SEPA was established and approved by NBM.The Application for adherence to SEPA was finalized and will be submitted by the NBM to the European Payment Council.

comment.narrative: By 31 may 2022 the Twinning Project team has continued to provide inputs in achieving the overall objective. Notably completion of the subresults 2.1 and 2.2 of the twinning fiche respectively the assessment of the draft primary legislation on insurance regarding the compliance with EU Solvency II Directive and related framework along with the assessment of the draft primary legislation on mandatory motor third party liability insurance regarding the compliance with EU Motor Insurance Directive resulting in a Gap Analysis Action Plan for the harmonization of the Moldovan legislative framework with the European requirements in the insurance area. In the context of activity 3.7 technical support in developing a methodology of a riskbased supervision of NBCOs in the areas of prevention and combating money laundering and terrorist financing was provided by presenting NCFM the model of methodology of a riskbased supervision of NBCOs which remains to be adapted by NCFM giving the country particularities. Subresult 5.1. was completed by providing an analysis of the state of play in Moldova and necessary steps for adhering to SEPA as well as other materials in respect to all components of the twinning project like training materials provided and assistance for NBMs staff delivered for designing a Macroprudential Policy Strategy GAP analysis prepared and recommendations prepared together with the NCFM staff in respect of necessary methodologies regulatory and supervisory tools under the new legal framework primary and secondary legislation for nonbank credit organisations training materials provided and assistance for calibrating debtservicetoincome and loantovalue limits structuring the Financial Stability Report as well as the framework to analyze household and nonfinancial companies sector presentations recommendations in respect to regulation of the financial market infrastructions questionnaire to address issues to payment service providers on fees for payments in euro and the infrastructure used to process these type of payments also to target the time needed to implement technical requirements for SEPA payments ISO20022 constrains and real commitment of the banks to adhere to SEPA as well as other materials in respect to all components of the twinning project. The activities of the project have been designed to support the achievement of the overall objective and its indicator and MS and BC partners are committed to support this process. During the technical assistance missions provided in the reporting period aspects related to institutional capacity are being taken into consideration from the perspective of sharing best practices and knowledge aiming to identify the best ways for the implementation of the experts recommendations. This is a step implemented before the dedicated trainings specifically addressed to institutional capacity will follow in the next period of implementation.

comment.narrative: Component 1The Macroprudential Policy Strategy was developed. The document was approved within the National Committee for Financial Stability on 15 September 2023. Two subcomponents of the stresstest modules were defined and are ready to use. Another component model has been developed and some additional toolboxes were purchased and the program was installed. An adaptation of the contagion model presented by the NBR STE on NBMs local data developed by the NBR STE in Matlab was done. An Action Plan for improving the quality of the FSR encompassing all the recommendations provided by the STEs during their missions was prepared. The NBM Board has approved the improved Financial Stability Report on the 8th of June 2023 and published on the NBM website on 15 June 2023.Component 2The assessment of the draft primary legislations on insurance regarding the compliance with the EU Solvency II Directive and on mandatory motor third party liability insurance regarding the compliance with EU Motor Insurance Directive and related framework was done. The drafting process on the NBM primary and secondary legislation in order to adapt to Solvency II Directive and MTPL Directives requirements is ongoing. The format of the missions along with the training are designed in order for the beneficiary instititution staff to address questions exchange best practices and gain knowledge. ASF experts assisted NBM in drafting a secondary regulatory framework for the external audit of the financial statements of the insurance companies including provisions regarding the endorsement of the auditing entity and the relation between the auditor and the audited entity andor financial supervisor. A draft of Risk Assessment Framework has been developed. NBM will prepare an initial draft of requirementsmethodology for insures undertakings stress tests.Component 3Necessary methodologies and supervisory tools were developed and enforced including guidelines for assessing the transparency of the ownership structure of the NBCOs and updating of information about founders ultimate beneficiaries regulation on responsible lenging offsite supervision internal procedure the Instruction regarding the financial reporting of nonbank lending organizations. Assessment was done for the fit proper criteria for administrators of NBCOs and criteria in this regard has been introduced in the primary law that amend the Law nr.12018 on NBCOs. NBM representatives have been trained during the missions dedicated to the capacity building of the NBM staff including through study visits. NCFM experts together with representatives of the Consumer Protection Agency have examined the best EU practices presented by the Romanian colleagues in the field of the analysis of unfair practices used by the traders in their relations with individual consumers. NBR STE presented the methodology for onsite inspections and offsite risk based supervision of NBCOs with the focus on AMLCFT. Component 4A number of 3 primary laws were amended and were approved on October 19 2023 by the Parliament of Moldova. A number of 7 secondary level normative acts were developed and almost all of them were already approved. All relevand staff responsbile with oversight was trained. STEs provided comprehensive presentations and guides on all aspects of oversight to all the NBM oversight staff. Detailed methodologiesinternal procedures to perform oversight following EU best practices were provided and elaborated.Component 5A comprehensive analysis of the State of Play in Moldova and the necessary steps to adhere to SEPA was done. A questionnaire in order to assess the level of interest and the readiness of the market players to adhere to SEPA was elaborated. An Action Plan with milestones and deadlines for adhering to SEPA was established and approved by NBM.The Application for adherence to SEPA was finalized and will be submitted by the NBM to the European Payment Council.
